title: Dong Son bronze drum
summary: Cast in bronze more than two thousand years ago in the river valleys of northern Vietnam, the Dong Son drum has a wide flat face with a many-pointed sun at its middle, rings of flying birds and ornament, four small frogs on the rim and flat handles at its chest. A padded mallet on the face gives a deep, wide ring that lingers.
howToPlay: The drum stands on a stone landing: the sun at the middle of the face, the bands of birds round it, the frogs on the rim.
Star is the centre of the sun, Band the rings of birds, Edge the outer ring by the frogs and Side the chest of the drum.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the slow strokes on the star, then add the bands and the edge.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: The pictures cast on these drums show feathered boats, wading birds, houses on stilts and rows of drummers. They are among the oldest records of daily life in the Red River region and one of the best known bronzes of Southeast Asia.
credits: Tradition: the Trống đồng Đông Sơn; patterns written for this game
